description: The configuration surface of the ferretdb chart. GENERATED from values.yaml by `./build.sh Charts` and diffed in CI — docs/plan/03 § charts/. Edit values.yaml, never this file. Members carrying `x-cybercloud-api: false` are chart or platform plumbing and are not part of the resource body.

backup.description: Backup to an object store, using CloudNativePG's barman-cloud. docs/plan/12: because it is PostgreSQL underneath, backup and point-in-time recovery are the operator's.

destinationPath.description: Object-store URL for base backups and WAL, for example s3://tenant-bucket/documentdb. Empty means no backup configuration is rendered, whatever enabled says.

enabled.description: Whether continuous backup and WAL archiving run. ⚠ Off by default, and only because there is no destination to default to: turning it on without a destinationPath below renders no backup configuration at all rather than an empty one, so the two properties have to be set together.

retentionDays.description: How long base backups and WAL are kept. The point-in-time-recovery window is this number of days.

gateway.description: The FerretDB gateway — what speaks the MongoDB wire protocol.

replicas.description: Number of FerretDB pods. The gateway is stateless — it translates and forwards, and every byte is in PostgreSQL — so this is a throughput and availability setting rather than a topology one.

gatewayImage.description: Override the full FerretDB image reference, tag included. Empty means ghcr.io/ferretdb/ferretdb at the tag `version` pairs with.
gatewayImage.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: One of TWO image overrides, because this chart renders two workloads and one escape hatch could not say which. A pinned reference defeats the version property, so both are platform escape hatches rather than tenant settings.

enabled.description: Whether both halves of this service are scraped: CloudNativePG is asked for a PodMonitor over the PostgreSQL pods, and the platform writes one over the FerretDB pods because FerretDB has no operator to ask. On by default — docs/plan/12: "a managed service the tenant cannot see the health of is a black box they will not trust with production".

nameOverride.description: Replace the generated object-name stem. Empty means derive it from the release name.
nameOverride.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Helm plumbing. Nothing about it belongs in a resource body.

platform.description: Resource identity injected by the reconciler. Not a tenant-facing setting.

apiVersion.description: The api-version the resource was last written at, rendered into the cybercloud.io/api-version label.
apiVersion.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

managedBy.description: Value of the cybercloud.io/managed-by label. Constant, and the selector every informer filters on.
managedBy.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceGroup.description: Resource group name, rendered into the cybercloud.io/resource-group label.
resourceGroup.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceId.description: Resource GUID, rendered into the cybercloud.io/resource-id label.
resourceId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceType.description: Fully qualified resource type, rendered into the cybercloud.io/resource-type label.
resourceType.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

subscriptionId.description: Subscription GUID, rendered into the cybercloud.io/subscription-id label.
subscriptionId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

tenantId.description: Tenant GUID, rendered into the cybercloud.io/tenant-id label.
tenantId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

platform.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

postgres.description: The CloudNativePG cluster the documents actually live in.

instances.description: Number of PostgreSQL instances, including the primary. One is a single point of failure and is offered for development only. Failover, replication and point-in-time recovery are CloudNativePG's, which is why this row costs 1.2 engineer-months rather than a rebuild of them.

postgresImage.description: Override the full PostgreSQL image reference, tag included. Empty means ghcr.io/ferretdb/postgres-documentdb at the tag `version` pairs with.
postgresImage.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Overriding this one ALONE is how a cluster ends up with a DocumentDB extension its FerretDB does not know. The pairing is in templates/_helpers.tpl and nothing enforces it once either override is set, which is why both are escape hatches rather than API.

sizing.description: CPU and memory per PostgreSQL instance, either by preset or explicitly. The FerretDB gateway pods are sized by the platform and are not affected.

cpu.description: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

memory.description: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 4Gi. Empty means take it from the preset.

preset.description: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Databases use the s1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 4 GiB.

storage.description: The data volume, per PostgreSQL instance.

class.description: StorageClass name for the PostgreSQL volumes. Empty means the cluster default.

size.description: Data volume size per PostgreSQL instance, in Kubernetes quantity form. Every instance carries a full copy, so raw consumption is this times the instance count. Grows online; never shrinks.

version.description: FerretDB minor version. ⚠ One property moves two images: the DocumentDB PostgreSQL extension and the FerretDB gateway are released as a matched pair and a mismatched pair is a proxy talking to an extension it does not know. FerretDB maintains no long-term branch, so the two values here are the two most recent releases and a third is a new api-version.
